author: reek
body: Loading a sidecar means parsing the on-disk JSON at codex.annotations/<quire>/<chapter>.json, routing each entry to the annotation store or the discussion store, and dropping the entries that carry too little to be useful. The old body loaded no sidecar at all: it built one Annotation by hand, added it to a store, and printed the count it had just put there.

author: reek
body: So this feeds one sidecar text holding every case at once -- two well-formed annotations, one whose kind is not in the vocabulary, one discussion entry, one missing its target and one missing its kind -- and reads back where each of them landed. Six entries in, three annotations and one discussion out, two dropped.

author: reek
body: Written as one literal rather than assembled, because the subject is the parser and an assembled string would be this test agreeing with itself about what JSON looks like.

author: reek
body: The malformed-JSON case is the control. load-sidecar answers the base fact unchanged when json-parse fails, and a loader that ignored its input entirely would answer the base fact too -- so on its own that case proves nothing. It carries weight only next to the good load, where the same call on the same base fact must move the counts.

author: reek
body: parse-sidecar and load-sidecar disagree on the same text, and the disagreement is recorded rather than smoothed over: parse-sidecar answers 4 where load-sidecar puts 3 in the store. Only load-sidecar routes on kind, so parse-sidecar keeps the discussion entry and buckets it to Discovery like any other unrecognised kind. A caller reaching for parse-sidecar because it looks like the simpler one gets a discussion filed as an annotation.
